extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions, with a multiple choice version and a direct answer version.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl; Nelson F. Liu; Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created through a two-step crowdsourcing process: workers first selected one of several textbook paragraphs and wrote a science question with its answer, then another worker validated the question and selected or wrote distractors aided by model suggestions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small percentage of passages could not be released, making the direct-answer version smaller than the multiple-choice version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks compiled from 28 books from online learning resources including CK-12 and OpenStax; paragraphs from these books were used as the base corpus.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Paragraphs from the textbook corpus were filtered using a rule-based document filter that classified sentences and accepted paragraphs if a minimum number of sentences passed rules targeting simple declarative statements.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers wrote questions from selected textbook paragraphs, and separate crowd workers validated question-answer pairs and created three distractors by selecting up to two model-suggested distractors and writing at least one themselves.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were quality-controlled by a second worker, who judged whether each question could appear in a school science exam; 92.8% passed. Workers included model-suggested distractors about half the time, resulting in 36.1% of final distractors being generated by the model.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The multiple choice version omits the associated passage, requiring systems to retrieve background knowledge themselves; the direct answer version is smaller because some passages came from unreleasable texts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and research for multiple choice science QA and direct-answer reading comprehension; also as additional training data to improve performance on real science exam questions.

name.evidence: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.

description.evidence: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions. This dataset has a multiple choice version, where the task is to select the correct answer using whatever background information a system can find given a question and several answer options, and a direct answer version, where given a passage and a question a system must predict the span within the passage that answers the question.

creator.evidence: Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions Johannes Welbl ... Nelson F. Liu ... Matt Gardner

inLanguage.evidence: We present a novel method for obtaining high-quality, domain-targeted multiple choice questions from crowd workers.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: In this section we present our method for crowdsourcing science exam questions. The method is a two-step process: first we present a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker, letting the worker choose one of the passages and ask a question about it. Second, another worker takes the question and answer generated in the first step and produces three distractors, aided by a model trained to predict good answer distractors.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The method is a two-step process: first we present a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker, letting the worker choose one of the passages and ask a question about it. Second, another worker takes the question and answer generated in the first step and produces three distractors, aided by a model trained to predict good answer distractors.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller, with 10481 questions in train, 887 in dev, and 884 in test.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We chose science study textbooks as our base corpus because they are directly relevant and linguistically tailored towards a student audience. While the number of resources is limited, we compiled a list of 28 books from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax, who share this material under a Creative Commons License.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We designed a rule-based document filter model into which individual paragraphs of the base corpus are fed. The system classifies individual sentences and accepts a paragraph if a minimum number of sentences is accepted.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To actually generate in-domain QA pairs, we presented the filtered, in-domain text to crowd workers and had them ask a question that could be answered by the presented passage. ... To actually generate a multiple choice science question, we show the result of the first task, a (q;a*) pair, to a crowd worker, along with the top six distractors suggested from the previously described model. ... The second instruction was to select up to two of the six suggested distractors, and to write at least one distractor by themselves such that there is a total of three.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk , requiring Master’s status for the crowdworkers, and paying a compensation of 0.30$ per HIT. ... We advertised the task on Amazon Mechanical Turk , paying 0.2$ per HIT, again requiring AMT Master’s status.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: The goal of this task is two-fold: (1) quality control (validating a previously generated (q;a*) pair), and (2) validating the predicted distractors or writing new ones if necessary. ... The total proportion of questions passing was 92:8%. ... On average, crowd workers found the predicted distractors good enough to include in the final question around half of the time, resulting in 36.1% of the distractors in the final dataset being generated by the model

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We used scikit-learn ’s implementation of random forests with default parameters.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Because the multiple choice question is trivial to answer when given the correct passage, the multiple choice version of SciQ does not include the passage; systems must retrieve their own background knowledge when answering the question. ... A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This dataset has a multiple choice version, where the task is to select the correct answer using whatever background information a system can find given a question and several answer options, and a direct answer version, where given a passage and a question a system must predict the span within the passage that answers the question. ... We also show that using SciQ as an additional source of training data improves performance on real 4th and 8th grade exam questions
